81883.subject: If Binance Isn’t Safe, What Is?
81883.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

It's been a while since I've done market talk, but this feels like a week worth discussing. Bitcoin closed its fourth consecutive week in the red, and yesterday's selloff suggests a fifth may be coming. The weakness hasn't been confined to crypto. Gold touched its lowest level in a year on Friday, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq sold off again yesterday ahead of today's midterms; Polymarket gives Democrats a 76.5% chance of controlling the Senate. It's fair to say October was a good month to hold cash.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/797f4e9b-67c9-475c-9c8d-3439447679d6/image.png?t=1793716335)
Caption: 

I don't know whether this is a bull market correction or whether the rally has run its course. But looking beyond prices, what concerns me most about crypto right now is security. Last Thursday, Nick Carpinito's [newsletter](https://blockworks.com/newsletter/0xresearch/issue/post_f505e795-45bd-4ae9-823a-28f0f4c4e0c6) covered the rise in crypto exploits: more than 300 this year, up 111% YoY. Talk about timing, as later that same day Binance suffered the largest crypto theft ever, about $6.3B, roughly four times Bybit's $1.5B in 2025. Yesterday, Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after about $40M in unauthorized transfers.

The silver lining is that both exchanges say customers won't bear the losses. Binance has already resumed withdrawals, with about $3.0B in net outflows over the past 24 hours and $15.4B over the past seven days, which includes the hack itself. Notably, Binance still holds about $125B in assets and has the balance sheet to absorb outflows of this size, which is encouraging, but I think there's a deeper confidence problem at play. If even Binance, the largest exchange in the industry, can suffer a breach of this scale, it's hard to imagine someone who doesn't spend their time in crypto feeling comfortable allocating to it.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b974053b-4a9e-4034-8133-8126e078019d/image.png?t=1793716335)
Caption: 

After this year's self-custody incidents, I would have told a friend outside crypto to just keep their funds on a large exchange. A [Coldcard firmware flaw](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/the-largest-hardware-wallet-exploit-of-2026-inside-the-usd-116-million-coldcard-hack) let attackers drain about $116M in BTC in July, and last month [tampered Ledger devices](https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-ledger-supply-chain-attack-october-2026) sold through a reseller were linked to roughly $93M in losses. 🟡 Model Deprecation

Gemini 2.5 Flash will be deprecated and auto-redirected on December 1, 2026

Gemini 2.5 Flash (gemini-2.5-flash) is being deprecated. Effective December  
1, 2026, it will no longer be available as a standalone model in the Gemini  
API or Google AI Studio, and all requests to gemini-2.5-flash will  
automatically redirect to gemini-3.5-flash-lite.

Action required for advanced integrations: While standard single-turn text  
and multimodal requests will continue to work automatically, you must  
review and update your requests before December 1, 2026, if you use  
function calling, custom multi-turn chat history, or custom thinking and  
sampling configurations.

Read Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite migration  
guide<https://c.gle/AGSJxQzDgWfEVWzWqAxjcCrW_mThdfXX6Uwg8A8x3CMXb2m8knzSIK14bI9hs1QRxZvfiP2XQJld3l_-om4IopQilZn3qHTyZfOl5fbBzwAVyX49eZL8O8vt1WIHMkg9aNG3L_iwG7xpfTCP47JoPX7jFGSxPDnksx-4-qkSK3mJEd5W0Uw_3Z1a2HSFWFlfhbtpQ1tLTrQHnq7Zl5fPjLV3EJKwa3944UFg5qfEBsth1EQBvLbEJdYvNzG90Q>

What this means for you

Starting December 1, 2026, your existing API requests to gemini-2.5-flash  
will route automatically to gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Once redirected (or as  
soon as you switch to gemini-3.5-flash-lite), your usage will be billed at  
Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite rates: $0.30 per 1M input tokens and $2.50 per 1M  
output tokens. That's the same as 2.5 Flash for text, image, and video, and  
audio input drops from $1.00 to $0.30 per 1M.

API changes to review before December 1, 2026

Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite enforces stricter API validation. Review your  
integration for these breaking changes before December 1, 2026, to prevent  
HTTP 400 errors and unexpected model behavior:

- Function calling and thought signatures: Multi-turn requests must  
preserve the thought_signature returned in prior model turns (automatically  
handled if you use the Interactions  
API<https://c.gle/AGSJxQy0z_6-f0mIXFn0NjzmhQ6XNrnQMqIm7tIPb70mkthZSCfWyCKL8F1Qm9XQzs2pgZVCWEiGtnQIAGgwQcj4496VPaAWT4hUA4V4pErSQPr-sgSI5cHWzhKdKlC6dZJmJrOR-n8I-UmVQFqHIMBa56kESLsxuCBVtMkgn86c_KYxInAzIlYYD084>  
with previous_interaction_id or official Google GenAI SDK chat history).  
Every FunctionResponse must also include the matching id (call_id) and name  
fields from the model’s FunctionCall, with any multimodal outputs nested  
inside the function response payload.
- Thinking configuration: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite uses thinking_level  
("minimal", "low", "medium", or "high") instead of numeric thinking_budget,  
and defaults to "minimal". For tool calling, code execution, or multi-step  
reasoning, set "medium" or "high".
